Under the single 'Format 1 (basic):' heading there are two consecutive fenced code blocks, each followed by its own paragraph beginning '> **Figure notes (PICTURE clause Format 1 (basic) syntax diagram).**' — the first block's middle row reads '⎨         ⎬ IS character-string-1  ⎢ EDITING character-1 ⎨     ⎧| NEGATIVE IS literal-2 |⎫  ⎬ ⎥ …' and the second block's middle row reads '⎨         ⎬  IS character-string-1  ⎢ EDITING character-1  ⎨       ⎧ | NEGATIVE IS literal-2 | ⎫  ⎬ ⎥ …'. claim.why_it_matters: One printed general format is presented as two, and the two renderings disagree with each other (different underline lists, different brace glyphs). A reader or a generator walking the markdown sees two Format 1 diagrams for PICTURE and cannot tell which is authoritative; the malformed inner brace in the second copy also misrepresents the FOR choice group's delimiters.

verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed on both sides, and the duplication is in the live spec file, not just the extracted work unit.

PDF side — rendered E:/Temp/specrecon/v471/spec_p471.png at 300 dpi (page 471 = printed folio 441) and cropped the figure band at 2x/3x. The page runs: '13.18.40 PICTURE clause' -> '13.18.40.1 General' -> '13.18.40.2 General formats' -> 'Format 1 (basic):' -> ONE diagram -> 'Format 2 (locale):' -> ONE diagram -> '13.18.40.3 Syntax rules' -> ALL FORMATS SR 1-5. There is exactly one Format 1 (basic) diagram on the page. Nothing between the Format 1 diagram and the 'Format 2 (locale):' caption. So the claim's characterization of the PDF is accurate.

Markdown side — specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 19948-19971 (mirrored in the work unit page-471.md lines 17-40) contain, under the single 'Format 1 (basic):' caption, TWO consecutive fenced code blocks, each followed by its own '> **Figure notes (PICTURE clause Format 1 (basic) syntax diagram).**' paragraph, before 'Format 2 (locale):' at line 19973. Both quoted middle rows in the claim match the file byte-for-byte (lines 19952 and 19966). The claim does not misquote either source.

This is not page-break furniture, reflow, wrapping, or formatting: it is a whole general-format figure plus its notes emitted twice, and the two emissions are not identical, so a consumer cannot treat them as a harmless repeat.

I also checked the two disputed rendering details against the printed glyphs myself rather than trusting either note:

1. Underlining. On the printed page the underline rules are clearly visible under PICTURE, PIC, EDITING, NEGATIVE, POSITIVE — and also under FOR (a distinct rule sits beneath 'FOR', separate from the PIC rule above it and clearly attached to FOR). Therefore the FIRST copy's figure note is factually WRONG about the print: it omits FOR from the underline list. The SECOND copy's list (PICTURE, PIC, EDITING, FOR, NEGATIVE, POSITIVE) is the correct one.

2. Inner FOR brace glyphs. Copy 1 line 19953 ends '⎩ FOR ⎩| POSITIVE IS literal-3 |⎭  ⎭ ⎦' — correct closing pieces. Copy 2 line 19967 ends '⎩ FOR   ⎨ | POSITIVE IS literal-3 | ⎬  ⎭ ⎦' — it uses the MIDDLE brace pieces U+23A8/U+23AC on the bottom row where the closing pieces U+23A9/U+23AD belong, so the two-row inner brace never closes. Confirmed malformed exactly as claimed, and only in the second copy.

3. Choice indicators (not disputed, but load-bearing and worth recording as verified). On the printed page a tall vertical bar stands just inside the left inner brace and a second just inside the right inner brace of the FOR group, bracketing the stacked NEGATIVE/POSITIVE alternatives. Both notes' choice-indicator reading is faithful to the print and must survive the de-duplication.

Net: the finding is real and was described accurately. The one thing the claim leaves open is which copy to keep — and the answer is neither wholesale, since copy 1 has the correct brace glyphs but a wrong underline list, and copy 2 has the correct underline list but a broken brace.
verdict.corrected_description:
REAL, as described, with one adjudication the claim left open.

Location: specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 19948-19971 (13.18.40.2 General formats), reproduced in the page-471 work unit at lines 17-40.

Defect: the PICTURE Format 1 (basic) general format — printed exactly once on PDF page 471 (folio 441) — is transcribed twice under one 'Format 1 (basic):' caption, as two consecutive fenced blocks each with its own 'Figure notes (PICTURE clause Format 1 (basic) syntax diagram)' paragraph, before 'Format 2 (locale):'.

The two copies disagree, and NEITHER is wholly correct, so the fix is not simply deleting one:
  - Copy 1 (lines 19950-19962): brace glyphs are correct (inner FOR brace closes with ⎩ ... ⎭), but its figure note OMITS `FOR` from the underline list. The printed page DOES underline FOR (verified on a 300 dpi crop: a distinct rule under 'FOR'), so copy 1's note misstates the print.
  - Copy 2 (lines 19964-19971): the underline list is correct (PICTURE, PIC, EDITING, FOR, NEGATIVE, POSITIVE), but its inner FOR brace is malformed — the bottom row uses the middle brace pieces '⎨ | POSITIVE IS literal-3 | ⎬' (U+23A8/U+23AC) where the closing pieces '⎩ ... ⎭' (U+23A9/U+23AD) belong, so the two-row brace never closes.

Correct resolution: collapse to a SINGLE Format 1 (basic) diagram using copy 1's brace glyphs together with copy 2's underline list (PICTURE, PIC, EDITING, FOR, NEGATIVE, POSITIVE underlined; IS, character-string-1, character-1 and the literals not underlined), and retain exactly one figure-notes paragraph.

The choice indicators must be preserved: I independently confirmed on the printed page that a tall vertical bar stands just inside each inner brace of the FOR group, bracketing the stacked NEGATIVE/POSITIVE alternatives. Per 5.2.6.4 that means one or more of NEGATIVE/POSITIVE, each at most once, in any order — not an exclusive either/or — so a single FOR phrase may carry NEGATIVE alone, POSITIVE alone, or both. Both existing notes state this correctly; keep that wording (dropping the inconsistent '900 dpi' / '600 dpi' verification asides, which differ between the copies and carry no normative content).

Severity 'structural' is appropriate: a duplicated general format is directly consumable by a grammar generator and there is no way to tell from the markdown which of the two conflicting renderings is authoritative.
